text: Hello everyone, welcome back to my class.Today, we are going to explore the topic of citizen journalism further.At the end of this period, you are expected to1.have a deeper understanding of the topic by completing a summary of the text2.appreciate the role and functions of exemplification in illustrating one's ideas through the analysis of examples used in the text3.Reflect upon how to be a responsible citizen journalist by working on the reporting of a new story.Now, please get your textbook and worksheet ready.Let's get started.Before we start our further exploration of the text, let's do some revision first.As part of the assignments for the previous period, you were supposed to complete the summary of the text.Please check your answers.Over the last few years, many breaking news stories have been recorded by citizen journalists.The camera work might not be perfect, but the content can be compelling.Equipped with smartphones, citizen journalists can provide news coverage more quickly than professional journalists.Stories posted by citizen journalists are usually more personal and have more emotional appeal, but they might not always provide background information or give a broad overview.Still, citizen journalism enables common people to share information to improve their lives.However, citizen journalism also causes serious ethical problems because it is largely unregulated and it is difficult to check the facts or trace sources.Citizen journalists can be easily tricked and may spread false information.Nowadays, citizen journalism is still finding its way.We should figure out how to make the best use of this kind of media.Have you got all the answers right?Hopefully, it refreshes your memories of the important points concerning citizen journalism.Now we will move to the deep reading part, where we will focus on the role of using examples in illustrating ideas.Please study the examples in the text and think about why the writer uses them to illustrate the benefits and potential dangers of citizen journalism.Let's look at the first example, the earthquake and the tsunami in Japan.Obviously, the example helps the writer show the benefits of breaking news stories being shared quickly, which is much faster than traditional journalism.After all, shortly after the earthquake hit, the videos appeared on the websites.The faster speed wouldn't have been possible if the reporting had been done in a conventional way.Now it's your turn to fill in the table.Please try to highlight how the use of examples helps illustrate ideas in your explanation.You will have two minutes for this activity.Ok, time is up.Now I'd like to share my thoughts with you.The second example mentions is a building that is burning to the ground.It is cited to illustrate the danger of citizen journalism.The writer worries that the online posts probably won't investigate how the fire started, who may have been affected, and what might have helped or delayed the effort to put out the fire.We learn from the text that citizen writers seldom cite reliable sources, nor do they typically provide background information or give a broad overview, which usually causes confusion among audiences.As for the story about an extremely dangerous online game and the false alarm of careless kidnapping, they are both intended to show the danger caused by citizen journalism.The example of reporting about an online game helps the writer show that citizen journalism can give rise to the spread of fake news causing unnecessary fear among people.The example of false alarm enables the writer to show one potential danger of citizen journalism in that scams and false information might be spread because posts are rarely checked and confirmed.When you compare example 3 and example 4, you will find they are both real stories, not made up ones.Besides, the victims are ordinary people.Actually, among them, they are maybe your parents, your friends, and the neighbors.And the harm done, whether financially or emotionally, is substantial.Why do you think the writers use real stories instead of fictional ones?The power of using real life stories is that it can make the message more compelling, especially for those who think the fake news or online scams are far away from them.Actually, my feeling went on a roller coaster ride, from being worried to being extremely shocked when I found the online game was just a hoax and the girl faked her own kidnapping.Then, I was really angry and furious.I can imagine the anger and hurt felt by the parents, who invested time and energy to keep children away from the nonexistent game, and the anger and hurt by the netizens who committed themselves to finding Kara.The two real life stories help to bridge the gap between the writer and the readers, and also help readers realize not only the serious consequences unconfirmed stories can cause, but more importantly, that citizen journalism is real and is affecting our lives in more ways than expected.Based on our discussion about the examples used in the text, we know that using examples is a powerful way to illustrate one's ideas, because it can support a general topic statement, explain a difficult point or unfamiliar concept, and help readers relate information to their own experiences.So, where words fail us use examples, that's the golden rule I hope you can take away.In order for the examples to better serve the purpose, they should possess certain characteristics.It goes without saying that the choices of examples make a huge difference in whether we can illustrate the controlling idea effectively or not.So, what are the criteria or standards for deciding on examples?Generally speaking, examples chosen to illustrate the controlling idea should be sufficient.Altogether, four examples are used in the text.The sufficient examples help introduce citizen journalism in a multi-dimensional way, covering both the benefits and the dangers.Of course, examples should be relevant.There must be a clear connection between the examples used and the opinion, the point, or the concept to be explained or justified.Examples should also be specific.A precise, exact, and detailed description is always desirable.In the first example, the writer gives a vivid description of the disaster scenes, like people climbed up the bridges and buildings, the tsunami swept the coastline, the camera work was shaky, etc.To help readers better appreciate how citizen journalism works.And why they can deliver news much faster and in a more compelling way.We've spent much time discussing citizen journalism.It's time to make connection with our real life.Have you or your friends ever reported a news story?How does the news posted by you or your friends influence your life?And why?Thank you for watching.Okay, time is up.Jenny, have you or your friends ever reported a news story?Yes, sometimes my friends post news stories on their microblogs or other social media sites.In what ways are you influenced?Their stories usually trigger a strong reaction and I identify with their messages or feelings more easily.Because on one hand, their stories usually focus on events which we care about, so the information provided is more relevant.Most of the time, they update news regularly, which means I can get useful information very quickly.Besides, things that happen to our peers or friends give us a sense of realness, which can better serve as a warning or a reminder.On the other hand, sometimes I read totally different reports about the same event.I don't know which one to believe.Thank you, Jenny.Just now, Jenny mentioned that in the era of social media, when every person can be a journalist and report news, sometimes there may be conflicting reports about the same event, which raises the question of how we can become responsible citizen journalists so that users won't feel confused not knowing what or whom to trust.Please take some time to come up with specific ways.You will have two minutes for it.Time is up.Let's hear what Simon wants to share with us.According to Simon, first, we should double-check the reliability of the news and make sure that the news is accurate.Simon, what do you think?First, we should double-check the reliability of the information.Yes, whenever we want to post information on social media, we should by all means confirm the truthfulness of the information.Second, we should respect and never invade other people's privacy.This is actually an important point many citizen journalists miss.You can't post pictures or videos of someone's life without getting permission first.Third, we should always obey laws and regulations.I guess we all agree that obeying laws and regulations is the bottom line.Apart from Simon's contributions, other students also actively share their ideas.Jenny said that we should avoid being personal and emotional when writing stories.That's true.Sometimes emotions may get in the way of us being objective and fair in our reporting.Lucy added that we should explore the bigger picture before we write and post the news.Yes, this is good advice to keep us from becoming a partial journalist.If you are doing the work of citizen journalists or planning to do it, please bear these good suggestions in mind.They will help you become a responsible citizen journalist.Would you like to try your hand and be a citizen journalist yourself?Please turn to many projects on page 10 in your textbook.You are going to post a news story.Think about some events in your local area that are newsworthy.Instead of doing it in groups, you will do it individually.You should consider the following factors.A local issue you'd like to cover.Sources you can use.Where you are going to post it.The main points of your story and its purpose.I will give you 30 seconds to read the model on the left.From the model, we know that the story covered is about a traffic accident involving an old woman on an e-bike and a passing car.The story should be reliable, as the sources are pretty convincing, which contain both pictures and the witness' description.The story can be accessed on microblog.As for why the news is posted, the purpose is to call local residents to obey the traffic rules.I guess nowadays, grandparents picking up kids from school is very common.Unfortunately, many of them do ignore the traffic rules, leading to increased number of traffic accidents.So the news is a timely warning to people, especially older people, they should not be above the law.Now it's your turn.You will have three minutes for it.The story is about a traffic accident involving an old woman on an e-bike and a passing car.The story is a timely warning to people, especially older people,
